## Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r7` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 1, 2, 2b, 4.1, 4.3 and R3 "Gameplay Designers" (Custom Item Designer + typed ability/event graph + verified component library); research `A-content.md` (items/abilities/projectiles are vanilla-client possible, high AI reliability) and `F-quality-market.md` (verified recipes over free-form code). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** One flag, OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (portal: a build request may get the designer route). Off, nothing is decided or recorded and every build request is byte-identical to before. **Not plan-gated** (owner decision): no plan lookup happens for the designer; any texture / sound / model a design references still goes through the existing asset gates (the texture route needs the top plan, sounds Saka+; without the asset the item keeps its base look / the sound key plays nothing). Installing and keeping are never gated. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the designer lives in `lib/cyrus/designer` and only uses `lib/cyrus/{datapack,engine-core,versions}`); no new tables, no foreign keys; designs are stored in the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "design"`.

**The idea.** Common mechanics (a weapon that marks enemies, a staff with charges and a projectile, a tonic with a timed buff) never need free-form AI Java: the model writes a typed `ItemDesign` (data), Nxeon validates it like code and **compiles** it deterministically into a complete Paper plugin that calls a fixed, reviewed component library. Every number, text and sound key of the graph becomes a `config.yml` parameter, so a later change of cooldown / range / strength / sound changes config.yml only: no regeneration, no model call, not one Java file.

### 1. Files
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/cyrus/designer/spec.ts` | the design IR (Zod): `ItemDesignSchema`, `CAPS`, `BUDGET`, `DESIGN_LIMITS`, curated catalogs, `designFeatures(version)`, `validateDesign` / `validateDesigns` (never throw: `{ ok, design, errors, warnings, checks, budgets }`), `budgetOf`, `walkActions` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/designer.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema, carries every cap), generated |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/components/java.ts`, `components/index.ts` | the verified component library (Java sources + metadata: purpose, families, limits, tests), the per-version `Compat` adapter, `libraryHash()` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/compile.ts` | `compileDesigns(designs, ctx)` -> plugin sources + plugin.yml + config.yml + README, deterministic; parameter collection (`designParams`), `nextConfigVersion` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/params.ts` | the edit path: `describeParameters`, `applyParameterEdits`, `recompileWithEdits`, `diffCompiled`, `planDesignEdit` (deterministic change-request parser) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/simulate.ts` | the TS reference simulator of the graph semantics (`DesignSimulator`, `JavaRandom`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/route.ts` | `decideDesignerRoute`, `matchDesignerWords`, `hasDesigns`, flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDesigns` (portal re-validation + re-compile, `serviceAgreed`) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |
| `services/modbuilder/designs.js` | service side: list/snapshot/check designs, asset keys of the workspace, `compileWorkspaceDesigns` |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-spec.js` | GENERATED bundle of the TS validator + compiler (734 KB incl. zod and the id lists) |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-example.json` | the prompt example (= the Void Reaper fixture, namespace `nx_abcd1234`) |
| `scripts/cyrus/build-designer-artifacts.ts` | writes the bundle + JSON Schema (`--check`, `--out-dir DIR`: run through devhost with an out-dir on node-2 and copy back) |
| `scripts/cyrus/designer-golden.ts` | prints the golden compile record (`test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`) |
| `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-designer-real.ts`, `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/` | pure suite, real node-2 runner, the three designs + golden hashes |

Changed: `services/modbuilder/{server.js,prompts.js,textures.js,Dockerfile}`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{request,sync}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/{create,types,client}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/engine-core/store.ts` (asset kind `design`), `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`.

### 2. The design IR (ItemDesign v1)
One file per item, `assets/designs/<id>.json`, at most 6 per mod. `{ schemaVersion: 1, id, base: "minecraft:<item>", name: {text, color?}, lore?, rarity?, glint?, assets?: { model?: "<ns>:<texture name>", sounds?: [keys] }, stats?: { damage + attackSpeed together, durability?, unbreakable? }, passives?: [{effect, amplifier?, slot}], marks?: [{name, durationTicks, maxPerOwner, glow?}], abilities: [0-6], permissions?: [{node, description, default}], recipe?, acquisition?: { loot?: [{table, chance}], drops?: [{entity, chance}] } }`. Unknown keys are refused. The item's identity is `<ns>:<id>` (PersistentDataContainer, never name/lore).
- **Ability** = `{ id, name, trigger, conditions?, actions, cooldownTicks?, charges?: {max, regenTicks}, manualCooldown?, manualCharges?, feedback? }`. Own cooldown and charges are checked before the conditions and spent when the ability fires (unless manual).
- **Triggers**: `right_click` / `sneak_right_click` (`targetRange?`: ray trace for a target entity + aim point), `left_click_hit_entity`, `kill_entity`, `projectile_hit` (`tag` of a `launch_projectile` of the same item), `held_interval` (`periodTicks` >= 10, main hand or inventory), `join`, `death` (fires for the dead player), `item_consume` (edible/drinkable base only), `charge_release` (hold sneak to charge, release by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; `minChargeTicks`, `maxChargeTicks`; actions may `scaleWithCharge`).
- **Conditions** (all must pass, `negate?` on each; a condition about a missing target is always false): `cooldown_ready`, `has_permission` (declared node `<ns>.<node>`), `target_is` (kinds player/hostile/animal/living and/or vanilla entity types), `world_in`, `health_below` / `health_above` (self/target, fraction), `item_identity` (main/off hand holds a design item), `sneaking`, `charges_available`, `random_chance` (java.util.Random seeded with `general.random_seed`), `time_of_day`.
- **Actions**: `damage` (player as the source: PvP and protection plugins apply), `heal`, `potion_effect` (31 curated effects), `knockback`, `pull_to` (self/point), `push_from`, `teleport_short` (self only, safe-spot search), `launch_projectile` (snowball/arrow/small_fireball/wind_charge; tagged, removed after its lifetime, arrows not pickable, fireballs non-incendiary yield 0), `spawn_particles` (28 data-free particles), `play_sound` (namespaced key only), `send_message` / `actionbar` / `title` (plain text + colour, `{player}` `{target}`), `give_item` (vanilla or own design item), `set_cooldown`, `consume_charge`, `apply_mark`, `query_marked` and `query_nearby` (bounded loops: target = each entity), `delayed` (one scheduled step), `branch` (if/then/else). **There is no run_command** and no way to express arbitrary code.
- **Recipe**: the data pack studio's shaped/shapeless shapes (`IngredientSchema` reused: vanilla item, `#tag`, list of items) plus own design items as ingredients (`ExactChoice`); registered by the plugin (a data pack cannot give the result its PDC identity); unlocked for every player on join.

**Caps** (inclusive; the schema refuses outside them, the runtime config loader clamps to the same numbers): cooldown 0-72000 ticks; charges 1-20, regen 20-72000; targetRange 1-32 blocks; held interval 10-1200; charge min 5-200, max 10-400; damage 0-40; heal 0-20; potion 1-1200 ticks, amplifier 0-4; strength 0-3 (blocks/tick), vertical 0-1.5 (velocity also capped at 4); teleport 1-16; projectile speed 0.2-3, lifetime 20-200; particles 1-64, spread 0-4, speed 0-1; volume 0-2, pitch 0.5-2; give 1-64; charge cost 1-5; mark 20-1200 ticks, 1-32 per owner; query_marked radius 1-32, query_nearby radius 1-12, max 1-16; delay 1-100; chance / health fraction / loot chance 0-1; time 0-23999; title fades 0-40, stay 10-200; passive amplifier 0-2; stats damage 1-40, attack speed 0.25-4, durability 1-10000; texts 120 / title 40 / subtitle 60 characters. Structure: 16 actions per list, 8 conditions, 6 abilities, 48 nodes per ability, depth 3, 4 marks, 4 passives, 6 lore lines, 64 KB per file.
**Budget per activation** (static worst case must fit; the `Budget` component enforces it again at runtime, so raising a query's `max` in config.yml cannot exceed it): 64 actions, 32 entity effects, 8 scheduled steps, 512 particles, 3 projectiles. No query inside a query; no delayed / projectile / teleport inside a query. Plugin-wide: 128 live one-shot tasks, 2048 marks.
**Semantic checks** (codes in the tests): banned bases (operator items, spawn eggs, ender pearl/eye, chorus fruit, milk, bundles...), block bases with click abilities, consume on a non-edible base, damage/attackSpeed pair, unresolved abilities/marks/items/projectile tags/permissions, reserved permission nodes, vanilla ids per exact version (items, entity types, loot tables, tags), foreign namespaces, missing target for the trigger, ambiguous sneak triggers, harmful/instant passives, recipe pattern/key, self-ingredient, plugin command name = a vanilla command, two ids mapping to one Java class. Warnings: item model on 1.21.1, unresolved asset keys, vanilla sound keys (not checked against the game).
**Optional-field defaults**: knockback lift 0.35, pull 0.25, push 0.35, amplifier 0, projectile lifetime 100, particle spread 0.3 / speed 0.02, volume 1, pitch 1, title 10/40/10 ticks, give count 1, charge cost 1, passive amplifier 0.

### 3. Verified component library (`lib/cyrus/designer/components`)
Fixed Java, rendered into `<pkg>.designer`: `Trigger`, `Budget`, `Activation`, `ItemIdentity` (PDC `<ns>:item`), `Cooldowns` (per player + ability, server ticks), `Charges` (lazy regeneration, no task), `Marks` (per-owner cap with oldest replaced, plugin-wide cap, cleanup on expiry / target death / owner quit or death / disable), `Tasks` (Paper main-thread scheduler only, tracked, capped, all cancelled on disable; timers restarted on reload), `DesignConfig` (jar defaults, clamping, migration hook), `Checks`, `Targets` (ray trace, nearby sphere, nearest first, never the player, no armor stands, players only on request), `Effects` (every action), `Ability` (the fixed activation protocol: re-entry guard -> own cooldown -> own charges -> conditions -> start cooldown / spend charge -> actions), `DesignItem`, `Designer` (the hub: owns all state, drops a player's state on quit and death), `DesignListener` (the safe listener base), `DesignCommand`, and the per-version `Compat`. Each component's metadata lists its purpose, families (1.21 and 26), limits and tests.
- **Listener rules**: observation handlers run at MONITOR and never change or cancel an event; they skip events another plugin cancelled (`ignoreCancelled`), except `PlayerInteractEvent`, which Bukkit delivers already "cancelled" for right-clicks in the air: there the item-use result is checked instead (DENY = another plugin blocked it). The two handlers that ADD items (loot tables via `LootGenerateEvent`, mob drops) run at NORMAL. Main hand only; one click activation per player per tick. The re-entry guard means effects of an activation (its damage, a kill it causes) never trigger abilities again.
- **Scheduling**: Paper-only (`BukkitScheduler`, main thread). No Folia region schedulers and plugin.yml does not claim `folia-supported`; `designFeatures(v).scheduling` is `"paper"` for every registry version (the registry has no Folia lane).
- **Commands** (plugin.yml, no Brigadier): `/<plugin lowercase> give <item> [player] [count]` (`<ns>.give`), `list` and `params [item]` (`<ns>.command`), `reload` (`<ns>.reload`); all operators by default; console can use all (give needs a player name there).
- **Config migration hook**: config.yml carries `config_version` and `# designer-values: <hash>`. When the jar's `config_version` is newer than the file on the server (the design's parameters were edited in Cyrus), every value under `items.` is reset to the jar's new default (Cyrus is the source of truth for designer values), the old file is kept as `config.yml.bak-v<N>`, `general.` is kept. A recompile with unchanged values keeps `config_version`.

### 4. Compiler (`compile.ts`)
`compileDesigns(designs, { version, namespace, pluginName, customHooks?, previousConfig?, configVersion?, assets? })` -> `{ files [{path, content, sha256, role}], readme, hash, params, pkg, mainClass, command, configVersion, designerValuesHash, modelsApplied, notes, javacVerified, libraryHash }`. Package `dev.nxeon.plugins.<lowercase name>`; main class; `items/<Item>Item.java` (ItemStack: `itemName`, lore, rarity, glint, item model through `Compat`, attribute modifiers keyed in the namespace, max damage + stack size 1, PDC identity; recipe; passives every 40 ticks; loot/drops); `abilities/<Item><Ability>.java` (straight-line Java: one field per parameter loaded by `load()` through `DesignConfig`, `check()` with the conditions, `run()` with the actions, budget checks before every action, `describe()` for `/params`). Items are sorted by id, so file order does not change the output. Deterministic: same designs + context = same bytes (golden hashes for all six versions in `test/fixtures/cyrus-designer/golden.json`).
**Per-version differences** (from the javap-verified API sheets + failure rules): `Attribute.GENERIC_ATTACK_DAMAGE/ATTACK_SPEED/MAX_HEALTH` on 1.21.1 (enum), unprefixed from 1.21.3 (registry interface; `designFeatures` uses 1.21.3, the registry's first plain version is 1.21.4); `ItemMeta#setItemModel` from 1.21.4 (registry capability `itemModelDefinitions`): on 1.21.1 the item keeps its base look and the README says so; `api-version` = the exact version; JDK release 21 / 25 from the registry. Everything else is the same source on all versions (each component's text is identical across versions; a test checks it). With `assets.models` given, an item model the mod does not have is left out (the item keeps its base look instead of the missing-model checkerboard).

### 5. Edit without regenerating (`params.ts`)
Every graph value is a parameter at a stable config path: `items.<item>.abilities.<ability>.cooldown_ticks`, `.charges.max|regen_ticks`, `.trigger.target_range|period_ticks|min_charge_ticks|max_charge_ticks`, `.<node>.<field>` with node paths `a<i>` (actions), `.n<j>` (inside query/delayed), `.then<j>` / `.else<j>`, `c<i>` / `.if<j>` (conditions); item level `items.<item>.marks.<name>.*`, `.passives.p<i>.amplifier`, `.loot.l<i>.chance`, `.drops.d<i>.chance`. Structure stays code: kinds, effects, particles, targets, stats, recipe, base.
- `applyParameterEdits(designs, [{path, value}])` checks each value against the parameter's caps; `recompileWithEdits(previous, edits, ctx)` recompiles against the previous config.yml and returns the diff.
- **Demonstration (test + real run)**: editing the Void Pull cooldown 160 -> 100, target range 24 -> 30, query radius 16 -> 20, pull strength 1.2 -> 2.0 and its sound -> `minecraft:entity.warden.sonic_boom` changes exactly ONE source file (`src/main/resources/config.yml`, `config_version` 1 -> 2) plus the README text; all 27 Java files are byte-identical, and in the rebuilt jar the only differing entry is `config.yml` (every .class identical, on 1.21.11 and 26.2). A structural change (a particle) changes exactly that ability's Java file and the config labels.
- `planDesignEdit(text, designs)`: a deterministic parser for change requests that only tweak parameters ("set the void pull cooldown to 5 seconds and the pull strength to 2", "change the void pull sound to nx_x:void_reaper.boom", "set the storm bolt cooldown to 40 ticks, storm bolt charges to 5"). Seconds are the default unit for ticks; `%` and hearts convert. A clause without a name inherits the previous clause's item/ability. Anything structural ("add", "instead", "make it shoot..."), unreadable or ambiguous (two items with a sound) returns `{ kind: "model" }` with the candidates. It is a pure API: the host can apply the edits with `recompileWithEdits` and skip the model; **not wired into `create.ts`** (decision below).

### 6. Reference simulator (`simulate.ts`)
A TS twin of the runtime: same activation protocol, cooldowns in ticks, lazy charges, marks (per-owner eviction order, expiry, death cleanup), the click / sneak / charge dispatch, the static + runtime budget, the re-entry guard (a kill caused by the activation logs `kill_trigger_suppressed`), delayed steps (dropped when the player left), held_interval timers, clamped config overrides (`config` option), and `JavaRandom` (a port of java.util.Random: the same seed gives the same `random_chance` sequence as the plugin; checked against real Java 21 on node-2). It logs effects (damage/heal/potions/velocity vectors/particles/sounds/texts/marks/branches); physics, real ray tracing, protection plugins and clients are NOT simulated.

### 7. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts` like the data pack route): with the flag on, a request with an item word (sword, staff, wand, tonic, potion, relic, bow, ...) AND an ability word (cooldown, right-click, charge, mark, pull, dash, teleport, projectile, buff, heal, on hit, on kill, passive, ...), `assets: ["design"]`, or a base build that has designs -> `service.assets.design = true` + the project namespace (a project is created if needed), `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.designer = { route, matched, limits }`. An unsupported version (26.3) gets a notice and no route.
- **Service**: `assets.design` parsed (non-boolean = 400; off with a note on unsupported versions); the `ITEM DESIGNER` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text; namespace in the user turn); allow-list `assets/designs/<id>.json`; a change build without the route keeps the base's designs byte for byte. Each round, BEFORE validate(): `designRound` validates every design with the generated bundle (+ the workspace's texture/sound keys); hard problems go back as a `design` repair (shared `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`); afterwards failing designs are dropped (customer-visible) and the rest re-checked; the valid ones are COMPILED into the workspace: generated sources replace every Java file outside `<pkg>.custom` and the plugin.yml / config.yml (free-form Java only in `custom/`, entry `CustomHooks.enable(JavaPlugin)` / `disable()`, wired into the main class when present). No valid design = the build fails clearly (never a half mod). Then the normal validate / precheck / javac / strict scan run on the generated code. `assetResult.designs` + `designCompile` (hash, config_version, settings, README, notes) + `designPromptVersion` `mb-design-2026-10-10.1`; `rec.config` lists the settings when the model's summary has none; designer builds are never deduped; `/health` lists `design`. The image needs `designer-spec.js`, `designs.js`, `designer-example.json` (Dockerfile updated).
- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `designer/sync.ts`): every returned design is re-validated and the whole mod re-compiled with the TypeScript compiler (the service's `configVersion`, `customHooks` and applied models reproduced); `serviceAgreed` = the hashes match; one manifest row `assets/designs/<id>.json` (role `asset`) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` (`kind design`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.item-design+json`, provenance = spec, compiler, library hash, compile hash, config_version, serviceAgreed, javacVerified) per design; `MbAssets.designs`. Idempotent like the other assets.

### 8. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-designer.test.ts` 75/75 (every one of the 39 caps at min/max accepted and just outside refused; 30+ semantic error codes; static budgets; JSON Schema current; components present + documented; golden hashes on 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11/26.1.2/26.2 and order independence; per-version differences; generated code free of reflection/threads/network/commands and clean under the strict source rules and the service's precheck rules for every version; config.yml/plugin.yml/README; custom hooks; unresolved models; parameter edits touch only config.yml; structural edit touches one Java file; edit refusals; the change-request parser; simulator scenarios for all three designs + permissions/negate/re-entry/runtime budget/clamping + held_interval/join/death; JavaRandom; TS == generated JS on fixtures + broken corpus for 3 versions; artifacts current; prompt section; routing; not-plan-gated request; portal sync). `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` 24/24 (4 new: designer build compiles the design into the workspace with the model's main + plugin.yml replaced and custom hooks kept, service hash == TypeScript; an out-of-cap value -> one design repair -> ships; a design that keeps failing -> dropped -> clear failure; not routed -> file removed, malformed flag 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite on the final code: 1279/1279 (an earlier run failed the image COPY test until the Dockerfile listed the new files, plus the known load-flaky `cyrus-admin.test.ts`, which passes alone). `tsc` clean.
- RAN REAL on node-2 (`devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-designer-real.ts --out ...`; raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/designer-r3-flights-2026-10-10.json`), one flight at a time:

| Lane | javac (27 sources, -Xlint:deprecation,removal) | Catalog (28 particles, 31 effects, 25 bases, 4 projectiles) | Jar | Strict scan | Test Flight | Edit jar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.11 / JDK 21.0.12 / Paper b132 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings (bytecode + source) | passed 6/6, boot 17.5 s, 857 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |
| 26.2 / JDK 25.0.4 / Paper b133 | ok, 0 warnings, 1.4 s | compiles | 70 KB, reproducible | 0 blocks, 0 warnings | passed 6/6, boot 13.8 s, 782 MB | passed 6/6; only `config.yml` differs; migrated 1 -> 2 |

  RCON evidence per flight: `plugins` lists VoidArsenal; `help voidarsenal` shows the plugin.yml command; `/voidarsenal` lists the three items; `/voidarsenal list` = `identity=ok`, the right material, ability count and `recipe=registered` for all three (so every ItemStack was built at runtime: names, lore, rarity, glint, item model, attribute modifiers, max damage, PDC); `give` from the console -> usage, to an offline player -> "not online", unknown item -> refused; `params` shows the defaults; an out-of-range config.yml (strength 99, cooldown -5, a bad sound key) + `/voidarsenal reload` -> clamped to 3.0 / 0 / the default key (logged as WARN, never an error); a config.yml with `config_version: 0` -> "migrated from version 0 to 1 ... backup config.yml.bak-v0" and the defaults back; on disk: config.yml written by the plugin and the backup present; no ERROR line from the plugin (4 sandbox no-internet lines, ignored by Test Flight). The edit flight boots the parameter-edited jar over the OLD config.yml: the plugin migrates it to `config_version 2` and `/params` shows cooldown 100, range 30, strength 2.0, the new sound. java.util.Random on JDK 21 printed the same sequences the simulator test asserts. Afterwards: empty `runs/`, no marker process.
- **NOT RUN**: no real Minecraft client and no bot: **gameplay behaviour was not verified in a game** (clicks, hits, marks, pulls, projectiles, particles, sounds, potions, teleports, recipes in a crafting grid, loot injection, passives); the simulator covers the logic, not the game. javac was not run for 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 26.1.2 (no resolved classpath on the build host): those sources follow the API sheets and the failure rules (`javacVerified: false` in every compile result); in particular the 1.21.1 `GENERIC_` Compat variant is unverified by javac. No real model build (fake CLI only, no paid AI): how well a real model writes designs is unmeasured. No customer server, no production DB, no migration, no deploy.

### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- One ItemDesign per file; at most 6 items per mod; the designer owns the main class, plugin.yml and config.yml; free-form Java only in `<pkg>.custom` (CustomHooks); custom code cannot add commands (plugin.yml is generated).
- Every numeric/text/sound value is a config parameter (auto paths), instead of asking the model to name parameters; structure stays code. Parameter defaults live only in the jar's config.yml (Java has the caps, not the values), which is why edits never touch Java.
- Designer values are reset on a `config_version` bump (Cyrus is the source of truth), with a backup; hand edits of designer values survive reloads but not a Cyrus edit of the same mod.
- `charge_release` = hold sneak to charge (no client mod, no experimental data components), released by right-click while sneaking or by un-sneaking; an item cannot have both sneak_right_click and a right-click release.
- Item-consume abilities run at MONITOR, so a cooldown does not stop the item being eaten (no refund).
- Stats (damage, attack speed, durability) and the recipe are code, baked into items when they are created (changing them later does not alter items players already hold).
- Unresolved own-namespace item models are left out of the jar; unresolved sound keys are only warnings.
- No query nesting and no delayed/projectile/teleport inside a query (bounded fan-out); damage uses the player as the source so PvP/protection plugins decide; teleport is self-only.
- `planDesignEdit` is exposed as a pure API and NOT wired into the build request: skipping the model for a change changes billing/revision semantics (a "build" without the service) and needs an owner decision and a service endpoint that rebuilds from edited designs.
- Designer builds that end with no valid design FAIL instead of falling back to free-form Java (no half mods, no surprise cost).

### 10. Owner actions (nothing needed to merge)
1. Decide whether to switch `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (portal) after a small paid eval of real model-written designs (not run).
2. Rebuild the build-service image with `designs.js`, `designer-spec.js`, `designer-example.json` (VM 88001 untouched).
3. Decide whether parameter-only change requests should skip the model (wire `planDesignEdit` + a service rebuild endpoint) and how they are billed.
4. A real-client test day (T): Void Reaper mark + charged pull, Storm Staff charges + impact, Vigor Tonic buff, recipes, on 1.21.11 and 26.x.

The Designer hub is shared, so touching Designer.java or DesignCommand.java to integrate menus/quests risks breaking golden hashes for item-only mods. I want item-only compile output to stay byte-identical even if the discriminator field is absent.

A better approach: keep gameplay features separate by adding new components to the `designer` package itself (like MenuManager) so they can access package-private DesignCommand internals without modifying it. Then I'd wrap DesignCommand with a new GameplayCommand that handles menu/quest subcommands and delegates everything else, wiring it in through the main class alongside the existing Designer.enable call.

The trickier issue is config migration — Designer's reload only migrates `items.` keys, but menus/quests need their own `menus.`/`quests.` key migration, and I can't touch DesignConfig without breaking the golden hash. Once DesignConfig.load() bumps the version and saves, there's no clean signal left for my code to know a migration just happened, so I need another way to handle that initialization.

I also need compileDesigns to partition inputs by kind, preserving the existing item-only path byte-identically when no menus/quests are present. Drafting the menu schema fields...

An entry needs an icon, actions, optional cost and permission. For the config-driven source, entries come straight from config.yml under a menu's entries list -- material, amount, price, name -- letting server owners add shop entries without regenerating anything, with buy actions fixed to charging cost and giving the item, capped at a reasonable max count.

The icon type can reference a vanilla material, a custom model asset, or a design item that displays itself, plus optional name, lore (max 6 lines), amount, and glint. Click actions include opening a menu, closing, or going back in the player's navigation history.

Other actions cover pagination, giving items, sending messages, playing sounds, triggering a design item's ability, applying potion effects, and healing -- essentially a trimmed subset of the AbilityGraph actions tailored for menus, plus quest actions like starting a quest or choosing a branch.

For costs, I'm working through a model supporting item, XP level, or economy costs -- the economy option only works through Vault when it's present on the classpath, but since Vault isn't a compile-time dependency and reflection is banned by the strict scan, I need to figure out how to safely reference the Economy class without breaking compilation when Vault is absent.

For the item-cost logic, I need to be careful about anti-dupe: charging must atomically check and remove before granting anything, all within the same tick to avoid races. I also need to exclude renamed or custom-identity items from counting toward a vanilla item cost, meaning I should skip stacks tagged with our PDC identity key and manually scan storage contents rather than relying on inventory.removeItem, since that matches by isSimilar and meta would interfere.

For granting rewards, I should check inventory space before charging and refuse the purchase with a clear "inventory full" message rather than dropping items on the ground, which means implementing a fits-check helper that simulates whether a stack of a given size can be placed.

Now I'm hardening the click-cancel logic in InventoryClickEvent for menus by always cancelling clicks when the top inventory's holder is a MenuHolder.

Only LEFT and RIGHT clicks (treating shift variants similarly) should trigger menu actions to avoid exploits, and only when the raw slot is within the top inventory. For drag events, I should cancel any drag touching the top menu, while move-item events don't apply since virtual inventories have no real location; I also need to close menus automatically on player disconnect.

I should also close all open menus on plugin disable and on player death, add a rate-limit so rapid clicks don't double-process actions, and schedule any menu open/close triggered from inside a click handler to run on the next tick using the scheduler, since Bukkit warns against mutating inventories mid-event.

For session tracking, I'll keep a per-player map storing their current menu, page, and navigation history, clearing it on close, quit, or disable—being careful that navigating between menus also fires a close event I need to distinguish from a real exit. Pagination size depends on the number of available slots, with next/prev controls shown only when needed, and permission-gated items should either be hidden with filler or shown as locked and unclickable.

Default behavior will show locked items with a red "Requires permission" lore line and refuse clicks with a message, using permission nodes declared in the menu's permissions list so the plugin.yml generator and validator can pick them up. For opening menus I'm considering commands like `/<mod> menu <id>` and `/<mod> menu list`, plus an `openWith.item` option that lets a specific item trigger the menu via right-click, likely through a PlayerInteractEvent listener for consistency with other item-based abilities.

Admin access would allow opening a menu for another player via `/<mod> menu <id> [player]` gated behind an "others" permission, with proper handling for offline players or console usage. For quest-type designs, I'm leaning toward one quest per file for consistency with other design kinds, keeping quest chains and caps in mind.

Capping quests per mod at 16 means total design files across items, menus, and quests come to 30, so I need to update the file count limit in the service to reflect that total rather than just the item cap. I'm sketching out the quest schema itself — fields like title, description, icon, prerequisites, and how the quest can be triggered (command, dialogue, or automatically).

For repeatability, I'm weighing options like once/repeatable/daily/weekly with cooldowns measured in seconds, and thinking through whether daily resets should use fixed UTC boundaries or a rolling 24-hour window since completion.

I'm deciding on a rolling cooldown approach instead of calendar-based resets, since it's simpler and avoids timezone issues while still being configurable (defaulting to 86400 seconds for daily and 604800 for weekly). I'm also sketching out the quest structure with 1-8 steps and optional branching paths (2-3 branches, each with their own steps and rewards) that can occur after a choice point in the main sequence.

Now I'm defining the Step schema to keep one objective per step for simplicity, even though parallel objectives per step could technically work. I'm also thinking through failure conditions (death handling, time limits, abandon permissions), rewards capping at 8, and permission requirements to start a quest.

For objectives, I'm sketching out the closed set of types -- starting with kill_entity (entity type, count) and collect_item (item reference, count, inventory-check or pickup mode, optional consumption on completion).

For inventory mode checking, I'm deciding to trigger re-evaluation on pickup events, inventory close, the /quests command, and step start rather than a periodic scan, to keep things event-driven and bounded. For craft_item objectives, I need to handle the tricky case of shift-click crafting where a single action produces multiple results, so counting needs to account for the actual result amount rather than just one craft event.

For visit_location objectives, checking on every player movement event would be too expensive, so I'm leaning toward a periodic timer every 20 ticks that only scans players with an active visit objective to keep the cost bounded.

For break_block, I'll monitor BlockBreakEvent and worry about the farming exploit where players place and immediately re-break blocks for easy progress—I could track recently placed positions in a bounded LRU set (say 4096 entries) as a rough anti-farm measure, accepting that it resets on restart.

For talk objectives, I'm thinking the simplest approach is just completing when the player opens the specified dialogue menu, regardless of how they got there.

For survive objectives, I'll check elapsed online time without death via a repeating timer every 20 ticks, resetting the counter on death.

I'm also setting count caps for each objective type (kills, collection stacks, crafting, breaking, survival seconds) and defining the reward types: items, XP, potion effects, and advancement grants that call awardCriteria for all remaining criteria via Bukkit's API.

For advancement rewards specifically, I need to validate that the advancement key exists in the project's own datapack rather than vanilla, so I'll check the workspace's advancement assets list and figure out the datapack file layout later.

Now I'm designing how quest progress persists on the player via PDC, using a compact versioned string format with quests separated by delimiters encoding id, state, step, branch, counters, timestamps, and completion counts — bounded in size and designed so removed quests are safely dropped on load.

For resilience, if the saved data is unparseable or an unknown version, I'll reset it but keep a backup copy under a separate key with a log warning rather than losing data silently. I also want step tracking to use step IDs rather than indices so that reordering steps between mod versions doesn't desync progress — if a stored step id no longer exists, I'll reset that quest to its first step while preserving its completion count, and clamp objective counts to the current step's definition.

Writing on every progress change is cheap enough at this scale, so I'll keep an in-memory map of player progress and persist it to PDC on each change rather than debouncing. I'm setting caps: 16 quests per mod, 8 steps per quest, 3 objectives per step, 3 branches of up to 4 steps each, and 5 active quests per player (configurable 1-10), giving a manageable total of tracked objectives. For dispatch efficiency, I'll register a single listener class indexed by objective kind mapping to the relevant (quest, step, objective) tuples. Now I'm sketching the command set: listing quests, starting, abandoning, and viewing info for a quest, plus admin commands.

Thinking through branching UX, I like having the branch choice menu open automatically when a player hits that point, with a `/quests choose` command to reopen it if dismissed. For permissions, I want normal quest commands open to all players by default, admin subcommands gated behind an op permission -- but I need to be careful that a top-level `permission:` entry in plugin.yml doesn't accidentally block regular players from the whole command tree.

So I'm deciding to generate plugin.yml without a command-level permission, and instead enforce per-subcommand permission checks in the command handler itself. I also want to add an actionbar progress indicator showing step counts when a quest updates, controllable via config.

Now I'm planning the new Java classes under a `designer` package: a `Gameplay` hub that owns the menu/quest managers, trackers, listeners, command wiring, reload/migration, and cleanup on disable, plus a `MenuManager` that handles inventory sessions, rendering, click/drag cancellation, and cleanup on close or quit.

content.content:
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

content.thinking:
I'm adding a kind field to asset design rows so I can tag them as item, menu, or quest, then generating a summary line like "Includes N menus and M quests" for the NxLabs mod page, keeping it focused on just menus and quests for now.

Now I'm sketching out the full spec: shared discriminator logic for designKind, then gameplay limits covering max menus, quests, slots, entries, pages, actions, steps, objectives, branches, rewards, requirements, and active quests — basically scoping out the whole constraint system before writing code.

I'm also drafting the gameplay caps ranges for rows, slots, amounts, costs, counts, coordinates, and cooldowns, defining valid min/max bounds for each gameplay value that will need validation.

Now I'm specifying the Icon type structure, requiring exactly one of material or item reference, plus optional name, lore, amount, and glint fields.

Next I need to define the MenuAction discriminated union, covering navigation actions (open_menu, close, back, pagination), item/message actions (give_item, send_message, actionbar, play_sound), gameplay effects (potion_effect, heal, run_ability), and quest-related actions (start_quest, abandon_quest, choose_branch, open_quest_log, complete_talk).

I'm also defining the Cost type for buttons, allowing item, xp_levels, or economy costs, and the Button shape with a fixed slot, icon, optional actions array, cost, and permission settings. I'm reasoning through how "talk" completion works -- treating it as simply opening the dialogue menu, which records the interaction -- and how cost is deducted from a button before its actions execute.

For actions involving give_item, I need to verify inventory space before charging anything, so I'm having the generated button expose a list of resulting item stacks, which the MenuManager checks for space before deducting cost and then running the actions -- establishing a strict dupe-proof order: cancel event, rate-limit, permission check, space check, cost check and deduction, then actions. Now I'm defining the list structure for menus, specifying valid slot ranges that avoid overlapping fixed slots and a source type for fixed entries.

I'm also specifying a config-based source with owner-editable defaults and a currency spec, plus prev/next navigation slots with icons and an optional empty-slot icon. I'm defining the entry shape (icon, actions, cost, permission, hideWithoutPermission) mirroring a regular button minus the slot, and the typed config entry shape with material, amount, price, and optional name, along with the currency options (item, xp levels, economy, or free) tied to a buy-only action -- deciding against adding a sell mode to keep things simple. I'm weighing whether config-source entries should be treated as version-resettable designer parameters, but landing on keeping the list config namespace persistent across version bumps rather than reset.

Now I'm settling on the list path naming convention, dropping a redundant key field since the path itself identifies the menu. I'm also sketching out the dialogue menu structure — speaker text, optional speaker icon, a set of lines, and a list of choices each with their own label, icon, actions, permission, and cost — and figuring out how a dialogue-style menu lays out speaker, book/lore lines, and centered choices across a fixed three-row chest layout, which leads me toward modeling the menu schema as a discriminated union between chest and dialogue styles.

I'm defining how menus can be opened: via command, via a designated item trigger, or via right-clicking an NPC entity tagged for a specific dialogue menu, plus an optional permission node required to open the menu at all. Then I'm starting to lay out the quest schema, including title, description, icon, prerequisite keys, and how a quest can be started either via command or through a menu.

Now I'm fleshing out the rest of the quest schema: repeat modes (once, repeatable, daily, weekly) with cooldowns, a sequence of 1-8 steps, optional branching paths after the main steps where the player picks one of 2-3 options, rewards, failure handling (death behavior, time limits, abandon option), and an optional progress bar. I'm also defining the shapes of Step (with objectives) and Branch (with its own steps and rewards) that make up this structure.

I'm now listing out the objective types (kill_entity, collect_item, craft_item, visit_location, break_block, talk, survive) with their specific fields, the reward types (give_item, xp, potion_effect, advancement, run_ability, send_message), and starting to explain how branching works once the main quest steps are completed and the player is offered a choice menu.

Thinking through validation rules: quests become unreachable if their start type is "menu" but nothing actually opens them, prerequisite chains need cycle detection to avoid circular dependencies, and talk objectives must correctly reference valid dialogue menus.

For daily/weekly quests, cooldowns are decided to roll from the last completion time rather than a fixed reset point. On the failure side, I'm defining onDeath behavior with three options — keep progress, reset the current step's counts, or fail the quest outright — and specifying that failed once-quests can be restarted since they don't count as completed.

For time limits, I'm setting up a periodic check (every 20 ticks, plus on progress updates) that fails a quest if it's been active longer than its allotted time, with abandonment allowed by default. For persistence, I'm designing a compact string format stored under a namespaced PDC key that encodes each quest's id, state, step, branch, counters, timestamps, and completion count, with state codes for active/choosing/done, and strict bounds on entry count and total string length to keep storage size predictable.

Now I'm thinking through migration safety: unknown version prefixes get backed up and reset with a warning, unknown quest or branch ids get dropped or reset to choosing, missing step ids restart that quest at step 0 while preserving completion counts, and counts get clamped to current target values so already-satisfied steps complete on the next check. I'm also making sure over-length data gets truncated by dropping the oldest done entries rather than refusing to write, and confirming the "q1" version tag is sufficient without needing a separate design hash since step ids already capture structural changes.

For objective tracking, I'm setting up dedicated listeners per objective kind: kill objectives hook into entity death events keyed on the killer, pickup/collect objectives handle both instant pickup and inventory-mode rechecking, craft objectives compute amounts from craft events, and break objectives ignore blocks that were player-placed by tracking a capped set of packed block locations from placement events. A repeating 20-tick timer handles distance-based visit checks, survive-time increments, time limits, and periodic inventory collect verification.

The timer and listener design stays bounded by only iterating players with active quests, and the whole system uses just one shared handler per event type (five handlers plus the timer) dispatching across seven objective kinds via an index map, rather than per-quest listeners. I also need to account for talk objectives triggered through the menu system, plus death/quit/join events handling failure resets, caching, and PDC persistence, before moving into reward distribution—giving items, XP, potions, and advancements, with a fallback log note if an advancement key doesn't resolve.

Quest completion needs to mark as complete and persist before rewards are given, preventing any duplicate-claim exploits if an error interrupts the process midway. I'm now sketching out MenuManager, which implements an inventory holder tracking the menu id, viewer, page, and page stack, with click handlers at different priorities—one to cancel clicks early in menu inventories, and another to handle the actual click logic.

Still writing click handling...

I also need drag handlers to cancel drags in these GUI inventories, plus close/quit/death listeners to clean up sessions properly, and I'm noting that InventoryView became an interface in 1.21 which should remain source-compatible either way.

For click types, I'm thinking through whether to only accept LEFT and RIGHT clicks or also allow SHIFT_LEFT, since shop-style GUIs often rely on shift-clicking to buy full stacks -- I'll need to decide how permissive the handler should be.

I also need to cancel every click and drag event whenever the top inventory is a menu holder, including clicks from the player's bottom inventory, since shift-clicking there could insert items into the menu. Since virtual menu inventories have no block location, hopper-related events like InventoryMoveItemEvent don't apply, but I should double check whether PlayerSwapHandItemsEvent (the F key swap) needs separate handling while a menu is open.

For defense-in-depth, I'm tagging menu icon items with a PDC flag so I can detect them anywhere they shouldn't be — then on inventory close, player drop, or pickup events, I sweep the player's inventory and cursor for flagged items and strip them out as an anti-dupe safety net.

content.thinking:
Compiling now, and next I need to run javac on node-2 to catch Java errors early. I'm writing the real runner test file modeled on cyrus-designer-real.ts, with a javac-only mode that builds including the vault jar on the classpath, then scans and does a flight test, making sure to add the VaultAPI jar path correctly to the classpath.

I'm mapping out the RCON checks GuildQuests needs to pass during flight: listing plugins, confirming item/menu/quest definitions, checking menu list output for shop and elder menus with their slot configs, verifying cost breakdowns per slot including the Vault-dependent money cost (which should be refused since no economy plugin is set up), and testing edge cases like console-only menu commands, offline players, and unknown menu names, plus confirming quest definitions like trial_two's steps and branches.

I also want to verify console behavior when trying to start a quest (should refuse since only players can do quests), run the quest integrity check to confirm handler counts and store roundtrip/migration/clamp tests pass, inspect the params output for shop and trial_one to confirm config values, and then test config clamping by writing out-of-range values (cost, count, max_active_quests, a bad list entry, an oversized price) and confirming reload clamps them back to valid ranges.

I also check guild_charm has params with n>0, then edit the flight by bumping shop cost count from 5 to 7, trial_one objective count from 5 to 8, and daily_bread's cooldown from 86400 to 43200 seconds, then recompile with only config changes.

Checking the jar entries confirms only config.yml differs, and the boot sequence overlays the edited jar on the old config so params reflect the new values. I verify the files on disk match, checking for backups and no ERROR lines, and note the RCON output is plain text that the expect logic matches as substrings.

Now I'm comparing the TS twin's progressEntryChars formula against the Java size calculation to make sure both compute the same byte-length formula for id, step, branch, and counts fields.

Checking the sample encoding: counts computed per quest as min(j+1, target) or zero, with fields for started timestamp, completions, last timestamp, state, step id, and branch, sorted by quest id — matching between Java and TS.

I'm planning to write the TS simulator (encodeProgress/decodeProgress, pagination, cost ordering, quest engine) first so I can validate the sample string, then build the real Java runner with all checks, running javac early to catch bugs fast.

Now I'm sketching the simulator's player model — inventory as item-key counts with slot/stack-size constraints, levels, money, permissions, online/alive state, world and position — and working out how to represent storage slots and max stack sizes per item type.

My simulator's approximation will be noted since real Java uses actual per-item max stack sizes. Now I'm starting to define the GameplaySimulator class, setting up its constructor to take the mod data and options like namespace, config overrides, click cooldown ticks, and max active limits.

Continuing the simulator design...

I need to mirror the click protocol exactly: cancellation reasons for wrong click type, slot position, missing button, rate limiting, permissions, inventory space, and payment checks, followed by action execution. The quest engine and codec should match the Java implementation precisely, including migration logic and notes count — now I'm ready to write simulate.ts.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

Now I need to write the unit test file covering fixture validity across supported versions (with 26.3 failing closed), confirming ItemDesign without a kind field produces byte-identical hashes to the golden R3 output, and verifying items with kind:"item" validate correctly—plus I still need to cover caps.

I'll build a mapping table from each of the 26 GAMEPLAY_CAPS to a setter function on a probe menu/quest, so every min/max boundary gets accepted and every out-of-range value gets refused. Then I need an adversarial corpus covering cost loops, arbitrage loops, reward farming exploits (talk-only repeatable with zero cooldown, collect-kept items), circular prerequisites, unreachable quests/menus/dialogue, oversized progress with many long quest IDs, excessive menus/quests, slot overlaps, too many pages, missing lists, opener conflicts, invalid talk targets, undeclared permissions, cross-namespace advancement issues, overly short time limits, unknown kinds, and schema rejection of unknown actions or arbitrary code-like fields such as "java". I also need to verify components are present in the compiled output, properly documented, version-independent, and free of banned elements.

I'm checking that strict scan rules and precheck pass cleanly across every version, that VaultMoney only appears when money is actually used, that item-only compiles exclude all gameplay components, and that Compat logic lives only in its per-version file. I also need golden hashes per version with order independence, and rules around editing without regenerating — price/count/cooldown/title edits should only touch config.yml and README, leave javaChanged empty, bump config_version, while structural edits regenerate the menu Java, with refusals properly triggered for out-of-range or non-parameterized changes.

Now I'm working through config.yml structure (lists, general settings) and plugin.yml permissions plus the Vault softdepend, followed by simulator behavior: shop pagination, click hardening against shift-click/number-key/drag actions, rate limiting, permission locks, insufficient space or funds blocking item/payment transfer, proper economy refusal without Vault, and quest flow details like dialogue triggers, kill tracking, item collection, event ordering for completion before rewards, prerequisite refusal timing, branch selection by visit, and survival-based quest completion.

I'm also mapping out cooldown and reset behavior for daily refusals and 24-hour retries, max active quest caps, abandon preserving completion history, codec roundtrip and migration handling for removed quests/changed steps/clamping/unknown formats, and verifying progressSample matches the TS encode/decode cycle.

Beyond that I'm planning TS-to-JS parity checks via validateGameplay and compileMod hashes across fixtures and broken corpora for three versions, prompt structure validation for the GAMEPLAY section and its limits, routing logic for menu/quest keywords with exclusions and flags, resolveBuildAssets behavior with gameplay-enabled services, portal sync validation including mixed design kinds and tampered quest rejection, doc asset line generation, workspace design checks with broken fixtures, and texture asset parsing for gameplay requests.

I'm reviewing whether existing test assertions still hold — the routing test matching sword/marks items, the prompt test, the sync test for asset kinds, and the regenerated JSON schema file — and considering whether to add a new pipeline test for a gameplay build using the fake-CLI pattern, modeling it after the existing designer pipeline test. With that groundwork laid, I'm ready to start writing the actual unit test file.
