cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r11 && cat >> docs/DOCUMENTATION.md <<'EOF'

## Cyrus menu and quest designers (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r11` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN R3 "Designers" (quest / NPC and GUI designer ideas) and RESEARCH-PLAN "Fourth document" 3.3 (Quest and NPC Designer) and 3.5 (GUI Designer). Extends "Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)" (same philosophy: typed IR, hard caps, verified Java components, deterministic codegen, every value a config.yml setting, no arbitrary code). **Nothing is deployed or switched on**: it ships under the existing OFF flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER`; off, nothing is decided and every request is byte-identical. **Not plan-gated** (assets referenced by a design keep their own gates; installing/keeping never gated). Host seam: no new Nxeon imports, no new tables (designs stay `CyrusProjectAsset` rows of kind `design`), no new asset kind.

### 1. Design files and the kind discriminator
Still one file per design at `assets/designs/<id>.json` (the existing `design` asset kind; the router, prompt, validator bundle, sync and Dockerfile entries are the designer's, extended). A top-level `kind` says what a file is: absent or `"item"` = ItemDesign (unchanged; `ItemDesignSchema` only gained the optional literal `kind: "item"`, so every existing item file validates and compiles byte for byte: the R3 golden hashes still match, tested), `"menu"` = MenuDesign, `"quest"` = QuestDesign. Items, menus and quests share one id space. A mod may have only menus/quests.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/spec.ts` | the IR (Zod): `MenuDesignSchema` (chest / dialogue), `QuestDesignSchema`, `GAMEPLAY_CAPS`, `GAMEPLAY_LIMITS`, `designKind`, `validateMenu` / `validateQuest`, `validateGameplay` (the whole mod: items through the unchanged item validator + cross-file checks), `arbitrageLoops`, `progressEntryChars` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay.v1.schema.json` | the portable MenuDesign / QuestDesign contract (generated) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/java.ts`, `gameplay/components.ts` | the verified gameplay components (Java + metadata), `gameplayLibraryHash()` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/compile.ts` | `compileMod(inputs, ctx)`: item-only mods go to the unchanged `compileDesigns`; otherwise items + menus + quests + main class + plugin.yml + config.yml; `menuParams` / `questParams` / `modParams` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/params.ts` | `applyGameplayEdits`, `recompileModWithEdits` (edit without regenerating) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/simulate.ts` | the TS twin: `GameplaySimulator`, `Pagination`, `encodeProgress` / `decodeProgress`, `progressSample` |
| `scripts/cyrus/gameplay-golden.ts` | golden record (`test/fixtures/cyrus-gameplay/golden.json`), `--print <file>` review aid |
| `test/cyrus-gameplay.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-gameplay-real.ts`, `test/fixtures/cyrus-gameplay/` | pure suite, node-2 runner, the showcase mod (2 items, 2 menus, 4 quests) |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-gameplay-example.json` | the prompt example (dialogue + quest + config-list shop) |

Changed: `lib/cyrus/designer/{spec,compile,route,sync,service-entry}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{request,sync}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/{create,types}.ts`, `services/modbuilder/{server,prompts,designs,textures}.js` + `designer-spec.js` (regenerated) + `Dockerfile`, `scripts/cyrus/build-designer-artifacts.ts`, `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`.

### 2. MenuDesign
- **Chest**: `{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "menu", style: "chest", id, title (32), rows 1-6, filler?, buttons?: [{ slot, icon, actions?, cost?, permission?, hideWithoutPermission? }], list?: { slots, prev: {slot, icon}, next: {slot, icon}, source }, permission?, permissions?, openWith? }`. `source` is typed, never code: `{ type: "fixed", entries: [clickables ≤ 54] }` or `{ type: "config", currency: item | xp_levels | economy | free, entries: [{ material, amount 1-64, price, name? }] }` (a shop the OWNER edits in config.yml `lists.<menu id>`; never reset by an update).
- **Dialogue**: `{ style: "dialogue", speaker, speakerIcon?, lines 1-6 (80 chars), choices 1-5 }`, laid out by DialogueMenu (speaker slot 4, lines on a book slot 13, choices centred in the bottom row). Inventory based on every version: Paper's Dialog API (registry capability `dialogApi`, 1.21.7+, experimental) is not used.
- **Icon**: exactly one of `material` (any vanilla item; display only) or `item` (a design item, shown as a copy WITHOUT its identity), optional `model` (own namespace, 1.21.4+), name, lore (6), amount, glint.
- **Click actions (≤ 8, closed set)**: `open_menu`, `close`, `back` (stack of 8), `next_page`, `prev_page`, `give_item` (vanilla or design item, ≤ 4 per click), `send_message`, `actionbar`, `play_sound`, `potion_effect`, `heal` (all on the clicking player; the subset of the ability graph), `run_ability` (an item ability of this mod), `start_quest`, `abandon_quest`, `choose_branch`, `open_quest_log`. No command, no other player.
- **Costs**: items (vanilla material WITHOUT a design identity, or a design item BY identity; menu icons never count), XP levels, or money through the allowlisted Vault API 1.7 (`lib/cyrus/import/deps.json` `vault-api`, compile-only, never shaded; plugin.yml `softdepend: [Vault]`; the bridge class is created only when the Vault plugin is installed; without Vault + an economy the click is refused with "This server has no economy (Vault) set up…"). Only mods with money costs get `VaultMoney.java` and the dep (`compileMod().deps`), which the build service puts on the javac classpath.
- **Opening**: `/<mod> menu <id> [player]` (unless `openWith.command: false`), right-click with a design item (`openWith.item`; that item may not have right-click abilities), or an NPC: right-clicking an entity tagged `<ns>.npc.<menu id>` (vanilla `/tag`; the interaction is cancelled so a villager's trade screen does not open). Quest NPCs = dialogue menus with `npc: true`.

### 3. QuestDesign
`{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "quest", id, title (40), description?, icon?, requires?: [quest ids] (≤ 4, a chain), start?: "command" | "menu", repeat?: { mode: once | repeatable | daily | weekly, cooldownSeconds? }, steps: [1-8 { id, text, objectives: [1-3] }], branches?: { prompt?, options: [2-3 { id, label, icon?, steps 1-4, rewards? }] }, rewards?: [≤ 8], failure?: { onDeath?: keep | reset_step | fail, timeLimitSeconds?, abandon? }, progressBar?, permission?, permissions? }`.
- **Objectives (closed set)**: `kill_entity` (vanilla type and/or kinds), `collect_item` (`inventory` = have it, checked on pickup / inventory close / the 1 s timer, or `pickup` = count pickups; `take` hands the items in when the step completes, all or nothing), `craft_item` (shift-click counts min(matrix stacks) x result), `visit_location` (world, x, y, z, radius), `break_block` (blocks placed by a player are not counted: 4096 remembered, not across restarts), `talk` (opening a dialogue menu of this mod by any route), `survive` (seconds alive and online while the step is active; death restarts the count).
- **Branching**: after the main steps a quest with branches waits in state "choose": a choice menu opens one tick later (`/<mod> quests choose <id>` reopens it), or a dialogue's `choose_branch` picks; then the branch steps follow; rewards = quest + chosen branch.
- **Repeat**: daily / weekly = a ROLLING cooldown of 24 h / 7 days after the last completion (not a calendar reset; no timezone); `repeatable` default 0 s; every cooldown is a setting.
- **Rewards (closed set)**: `give_item` (overflow drops at the feet), `xp` (points or levels), `potion_effect`, `advancement` (only `<ns>:<path>` of THIS project's data pack; the service checks the workspace's `assets/datapack` specs; a missing one at runtime logs once and grants nothing), `run_ability`, `send_message`.
- **Commands**: `/<mod> quests` (players: their quests and states; console: definitions), `quests log` (GUI), `quests start|abandon|info|choose <id>`, `quests list`, `quests check` (ops), `quests reset <player>` (`<ns>.quests.admin`). Progress on the actionbar when it changes (unless `progressBar: false`).
- **Progress persistence (QuestStore)**: the player's PersistentDataContainer `<ns>:quests` (saved with the player file, no database), versioned text `q1|<quest>,<A|C|D>,<step id>,<branch id>,<c0>.<c1>.<c2>,<started>,<completions>,<last>|…` sorted by quest id, at most 2048 characters per player per mod (the validator proves the worst case fits: `progress_oversize`). Migration-safe against the CURRENT definitions: unknown format -> copied to `<ns>:quests_backup` and reset; removed quests dropped; a step or branch that no longer exists restarts that quest (completions kept); counts clamped to the current targets. The TS codec is identical (checked on the real JVM, below).

### 4. Caps and limits
`GAMEPLAY_CAPS` (inclusive; schema refuses outside, runtime config loader clamps to the same): rows 1-6; slot 0-53; icon amount 1-64; item cost 1-2304; XP level cost 1-1000; money 0.01-1,000,000; give 1-64; heal 0-20; potion 1-1200 ticks, amplifier 0-4; volume 0-2, pitch 0.5-2; kill 1-1000; collect 1-2304; craft 1-1000; break 1-10000; survive 10-7200 s; visit radius 1-64; x/z ±30,000,000, y ±2048; repeat cooldown 0-2,592,000 s; time limit 60-604,800 s; XP points 1-100,000, levels 1-100; config-list amount 1-64; `general.menu_click_cooldown_ticks` 2-40 (runtime). `GAMEPLAY_LIMITS`: 8 menus, 16 quests, 30 design files per mod (6 items as before), 54 buttons, 45 list slots, 54 fixed entries, 270 config entries, 10 pages, 8 actions per click, 5 choices, 6 lines, 8 steps, 3 objectives per step, 3 branches of ≤ 4 steps, 8 rewards, 4 prerequisites, back stack 8, active quests per player `general.max_active_quests` 1-5 (default 3; so ≤ 15 tracked objectives per player), 2048 progress characters. Listeners: ONE ObjectiveTracker (9 handlers, one per event kind) + one shared 1 s timer per mod, never one per quest.

**Validation (codes tested)**: closed sets + unknown keys (no `run_command`, no code fields), slots outside / overlapping, too many pages, `no_list` (page actions without a list), `cost_loop` (a click giving more of its own cost item; a config list selling its currency), `arbitrage_loop` (an exchange-rate cycle over every priced click, config-list default and fast-repeat hand-in quest whose product is > 1: Bellman-Ford on -log rates), `cost_without_action`, `too_many_gives`, `reward_farm` (a repeat with cooldown < 60 s that completes instantly (talk/visit only) and gives items/XP, or asks to HAVE X and rewards X), `circular_prerequisites`, `unreachable_menu` (no command, item, NPC or open_menu from an openable menu), `unreachable_quest` (start "menu" without a start_quest in an openable menu, or a prerequisite that can never start), `unreachable_dialogue`, `not_dialogue`, `not_craftable` (design item without a recipe), `time_limit_too_short`, `progress_oversize`, `opener_conflict`, `undeclared_permission`, `reserved_node` (give, reload, command, list, params, menu, quests, npc), `advancement_not_in_project`, `foreign_namespace`, `banned_item` (gives/costs; icons are display-only and may be any item), `icon_source`, `unknown_kind`, per-kind counts. Warnings: money needs Vault, vanilla sound keys unchecked, unresolved models, `run_ability_no_target`.

### 5. Verified component library (gameplay)
In `<pkg>.designer` next to the 17 item components (they use the Designer hub: identity, tasks, config, abilities): `Gameplay` (hub: own clamping DesignConfig, menus.* / quests.* migration, icons, cleanup), `MenuDef`, `MenuContext`, `MenuManager`, `Pagination`, `CostCharger`, `DialogueMenu`, `QuestDef`, `QuestStore`, `Quests`, `ObjectiveTracker`, `RewardDistributor`, `GameplayCommand`, plus `VaultMoney` only with money costs. No per-version code (the item library's `Compat` stays the only per-version file; tested). Each has metadata (purpose, families 1.21 + 26, limits, tests).
- **MenuManager hardening**: a menu inventory is recognised only by its `InventoryHolder` (never by title). EVERY `InventoryClickEvent` and `InventoryDragEvent` whose top inventory is a menu is cancelled at LOWEST (others see it cancelled) and again at HIGHEST (nobody un-cancels it before MONITOR): clicks in the player's own inventory, shift-clicks, number keys, off-hand swap, double click, drop, middle/creative clicks and drags do nothing. Only a plain LEFT or RIGHT click on a menu slot runs a button, once per `menu_click_cooldown_ticks` per player, in the fixed order **permission -> room for every given stack (simulated on a copy) -> can pay -> TAKE (re-checked, all or nothing) -> actions**. Icons carry `<ns>:menu_icon` and never a design identity; a flagged stack on the cursor or in the inventory when a menu closes (or dropped) is removed. Navigation runs one tick later (never inside the click event). Per-player state (open menu, page, back stack) dropped on close, quit and death; all menus closed on disable.
- **Quests**: completion is STORED (PDC) before any reward is given, so a reward can never be claimed twice; start rules = permission, prerequisites (completed once), repeat rule, active cap, size cap.
- **Config**: `general.*` (seed, click cooldown, max active quests) and `lists.*` (owner shop lines) are never reset; on a `config_version` bump the item loader resets `items.*` (with the backup) and `Gameplay` resets `menus.*` and `quests.*` (it reads the on-disk version before the item loader migrates). Config lists are checked on load: unknown/banned materials skipped, prices clamped per currency, a list selling its own currency skipped, at most 10 pages / 270 entries; each problem is a reload note.
- **plugin.yml** (menu/quest mods): the command has NO plugin.yml permission gate (players must reach `/<mod> menu` and `/<mod> quests`); per-subcommand nodes: `<ns>.command`, `.give`, `.reload`, `.menu.others`, `.quests.admin` (op), `<ns>.menu`, `<ns>.quests` (true), plus declared design permissions.

### 6. Compiler and edit without regenerating
`compileMod` emits the item components + gameplay components + `items/`, `abilities/`, `menus/<Id>Menu.java`, `quests/<Id>Quest.java` (straight-line `load()` / `rewards()` calls; no interpreter), the main class (Designer + Gameplay; ModelStates wiring from feature/cyrus-r2 when items have states), plugin.yml, config.yml (`general`, `items`, `menus`, `quests`, `lists`), README (items, menus with prices, quests with steps and paths, settings, commands, notes). Deterministic, order-independent, golden hashes for 1.21.1 / 1.21.4 / 1.21.8 / 1.21.11 / 26.1.2 / 26.2. Parameter paths: `menus.<id>.title|speaker|line<i>`, `.b<slot>|e<i>|c<i>|prev|next` + `.name|lore<j>|amount|cost.count|cost.levels|cost.amount|a<k>.<field>`; `quests.<id>.title|description|icon.*|repeat.cooldown_seconds|failure.time_limit_seconds|branches.prompt|branches.<b>.label|steps.<step>.text|steps.<step>.o<j>.count|seconds|world|x|y|z|radius|rewards.r<i>.*|branches.<b>.rewards.r<i>.*`. `recompileModWithEdits` checks each value against its caps; item paths go through the item edit path.
- **Demonstration**: price 5 -> 7 (`menus.shop.b47.cost.count`), kills 5 -> 8 (`quests.trial_one.steps.s1.o0.count`), daily cooldown 86400 -> 43200 s: on 1.21.11 and 26.2 exactly ONE source file changed (`src/main/resources/config.yml`, config_version 1 -> 2) + the README; in the rebuilt jar the only differing entry is `config.yml`, all 63 `.class` files identical; the edited jar booted over the OLD config.yml migrated it and `/guildquests params` / `quests list` / `menu costs` showed 7, 8, 43200. Pure tests also edit a money price, a coordinate, a dialogue line and an item cooldown at once (config.yml only); a structural edit (one more action on a button) changes exactly `ShopMenu.java` + config.yml.

### 7. Build service, router, portal
- **Router** (`route.ts`): with `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1`, menu words (gui, menu, shop, selector, kit menu, dialogue, NPC dialogue…) or quest words (quest, quest chain, quest giver, mission, daily/weekly task/quest, bounty) route to the designer with `gameplay: { menus, quests }`; requests the IR cannot honestly express get NO gameplay route (auction house, player-to-player trading, player/chest/sign shops, banks, claims, minigames, leaderboards, databases, webhooks, Discord). A base build with menu/quest design rows keeps the part (`hasGameplayDesigns`, `existingGameplay` from `create.ts`). Request: `service.gameplay = true` only with `design`; meta `designer.gameplay`.
- **Service**: `assets.gameplay` (boolean, needs `design`; else 400); the `MENUS AND QUESTS` prompt part is appended after the ITEM DESIGNER section only when `design && gameplay` (fixed text + example; otherwise the prompt is byte-identical); `checkWorkspaceDesigns` validates the whole mod with `validateGameplay` from the generated bundle (per-kind caps; a file blamed by a cross-file error is dropped after the bounded repairs, the rest re-checked); `compileWorkspaceDesigns` uses `compileMod` (summary + `counts`, `deps`); `vault-api` joins the javac classpath only when the compile needs it (a missing jar = a clear "dependency not available" failure); prompt version `mb-design-2026-10-10.1+mb-gameplay-2026-10-10.1`; asset results carry `kind`.
- **Portal sync**: `checkReturnedDesigns` re-validates every kind together and re-compiles with `compileMod` (`serviceAgreed` by hash); `CyrusProjectAsset` mime per kind (`application/vnd.nxeon.{item,menu,quest}-design+json`), provenance `designKind` for menus/quests; `MbAssets.designs[].kind`; revision message "N item designs + N menus + N quests". - Quest progress lives in the player's PDC (no database, no Cyrus table); a changed step restarts that quest; abandoning or failing keeps the completion history; a failed quest with no completion is simply removed.

- **Rewards (closed set)**: `give_item` (overflow drops at the feet), `xp` (points or levels), `potion_effect`, `advancement` (only `<ns>:<path>` of THIS project's data pack; the service checks the workspace's `assets/datapack` specs; a missing one at runtime logs once and grants nothing), `run_ability`, `send_message`.

### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- No new asset kind: a `kind` field on the existing design files; item files without it are unchanged byte for byte. Items, menus and quests share one id space; 30 files per mod.
- One quest per file; dialogues are menus (`style: "dialogue"`), and "talk" = opening that dialogue by any route; NPCs are any entity with the scoreboard tag `<ns>.npc.<menu id>` (no NPC entity designer yet).
- Inventory-based dialogues on every version instead of Paper's experimental Dialog API (1.21.7+).
- Only plain left/right clicks act (shift-click "buy a stack" deliberately unsupported); a purchase is refused when the inventory lacks room (nothing is dropped); quest rewards drop overflow at the feet instead (a reward must not be lost).
- Vanilla item costs count only stacks without a design identity (a design item based on emerald never pays an emerald price); icons never count.
- Config lists (owner shop lines) live under `lists.*` and are never reset by an update; everything else a design sets is a designer value (reset on a config_version bump, with the backup).
- Daily/weekly are rolling cooldowns (24 h / 7 days after the last completion), not calendar resets.
- Quest progress lives in the player's PDC (no database, no Cyrus table); a changed step restarts that quest; abandoning or failing keeps the completion history; a failed quest with no completion is simply removed.
- Fast-repeat instant quests may not give items/XP (cooldown < 60 s); arbitrage is checked across all priced clicks of the mod at the design level and again for owner config lists at runtime (a list cannot sell its own currency).
- Menu/quest mods drop the plugin.yml command permission gate (players need the command); admin subcommands keep op-default nodes.
- `planDesignEdit` (the deterministic change-request parser) still covers item parameters only; menu/quest edits go through `applyGameplayEdits` / `recompileModWithEdits` by exact path (not wired into `create.ts`, same owner decision as before).

The menu and quest designers are built and committed on `feature/cyrus-r11` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r11`). Real flights passed on 1.21.11 and 26.2. Nothing is deployed or switched on; it all sits behind the `CYRUS_DESIGNER` flag, which stays off.

**What I built:** `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/{spec,java,components,compile,params,simulate}.ts`, `gameplay.v1.schema.json`, `scripts/cyrus/gameplay-golden.ts`, `test/cyrus-gameplay.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-gameplay-real.ts`, fixtures in `test/fixtures/cyrus-gameplay/` and `services/modbuilder/designer-gameplay-example.json`. I extended the existing designer route, request, meta, sync, mod-page lines and the service code (`server`, `prompts`, `designs`, `textures`, Dockerfile, regenerated `designer-spec.js`). Design files stay `assets/designs/<id>.json` with a new `kind` field. Item files without it compile byte-identically (the R3 golden hashes still match).

**Ran:**
- `tsc` is clean; 61 new pure tests pass, plus 2 pipeline tests.
- The full Cyrus + modbuilder suite passes (1531/1531) after merging `feature/cyrus-r2` twice.
- On node-2, both lanes compiled with zero javac warnings, the jars are reproducible and the strict scan found nothing.
- Each Test Flight ran 21 RCON checks: commands, `menu list`, `menu costs` (a money price is refused cleanly without Vault), the quest progress format checked on the server's Java (output identical to the TypeScript twin), clamping and config migration.
- Results file: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/gameplay-r11-flights-2026-10-10.json`.

**Not run:** no Minecraft client or bot. Clicking menus, the click hardening, NPC/item openers and quest progress from real play are not verified. Money payment is untested because there was no Vault + economy plugin on the server. Other versions are not javac-checked, and no real model build was done.

**Caps and components:** 8 menus, 16 quests, 6 slot rows, 10 pages, 8 actions per click, 8 steps × 3 objectives, 1–5 active quests per player, 2048 characters of stored progress per player, and one shared listener per mod. Components: MenuManager, Pagination, CostCharger, DialogueMenu, QuestStore, Quests, ObjectiveTracker, RewardDistributor, Gameplay, MenuDef, MenuContext, QuestDef, GameplayCommand, and VaultMoney only when a mod has money prices.

- Quest progress is stored on the player; a changed step restarts that quest.
- Menu/quest mods remove the command's plugin.yml permission gate so players can use it.
